blocks.in: The one-time return of advice under the 44th Amendment; Article 78's duty on the PM to inform.
blocks.w: The President's real powers are **informational and residual**, not executive.

blocks.x: Secretariat assistance to the Cabinet, **inter-ministerial coordination**, and allocation of business under **Article 77(3)**.

blocks.in: The **Cabinet Secretary** is the senior-most civil servant, chairs the Civil Services Board and the **National Crisis Management Committee**.
blocks.w: It coordinates by **convening**, not by commanding — its authority is derived.

blocks.x: An **extra-constitutional** body with no allocated business of its own, assisting the PM under Article 78.

blocks.w: The **PMO versus Cabinet Secretariat** debate is really about whether coordination should be political or institutional.

blocks.in: **ACC** for appointments, **CCS** for security and defence acquisitions, **CCEA**, **CCPA**, and committees on investment and employment.
blocks.w: The full Cabinet often **ratifies what a committee has decided**.

blocks.in: Secretary → Additional/Special → Joint Secretary → Director/Deputy → Under Secretary → Section Officer; the **Joint Secretary is the pivot**.
blocks.w: The **secretariat-executive gap** — policy written by those who never ran a field office — is the standing criticism.

blocks.w: Design questions are always the same five: **appointment, tenure, funding, separation of roles, appeal**.

blocks.t: NITI Aayog and the Planning Commission
blocks.x: An allocative body replaced by a **think tank with no financial powers**.

blocks.w: NITI persuades through **data and ranking**, where the Commission commanded through **money**.
